venue_now: arXiv:2407.15240v6, 31 Mar 2025 (p.1); the text shows no venue
what_it_is: BIGbench (Biases of Image Generation benchmark) measures social bias in text-to-image models; it is not a language-model reasoning suite (p.1). It defines bias along four dimensions (acquired attribute, protected attribute, manifestation, visibility) and builds 47,040 prompts from occupations, social relations and characteristics combined with sex, race and age (pp.2-4). Images generated by the evaluated models are labelled by a fine-tuned multimodal LLM aligner (Mini-InternVL-4B 1.5) and scored with implicit and explicit bias scores and a manifestation factor (pp.4-6). It evaluates 8 text-to-image models and 3 debiasing methods (p.2, p.6).
domain: social bias in text-to-image generation (computer vision, fairness)
size: 47,040 prompts; 8 text-to-image models and 3 debiasing methods; 1,000 human-labelled images to validate the aligner (p.2, p.6)
source_of_items: prompts constructed by the authors from attribute lists (179 occupations in 15 categories, 11 sets of social relations, 12 antonym pairs of characteristics) combined with protected attributes (pp.3-4)
instances: static prompt set; the images are generated by the evaluated models, 8 per prompt (p.6)
evaluation: automated: a fine-tuned multimodal LLM identifies sex, race and age in generated images, and bias scores are computed against demographic statistics (pp.4-6)
human_validation: Ten trained annotators of different races labelled 1,000 generated images as ground truth for the aligner; the fine-tuned InternVL reached 97.93% average alignment accuracy (sex 100, race 98.6, age 95.2) (p.6, Table 2).

engtrace_use.sentence: S-E1 (L182-190): 'Generalist suites like MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021a), BIG-Bench (Luo et al., 2024), and SuperGPQA (Du et al., 2025) restrict assessment to factual recall via multiple-choice questions, ...'
engtrace_use.explanation: The citation points at the wrong paper. Luo et al. (2024) is 'BIGbench: A Unified Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-dimensional Social Biases in Text-to-Image Models' (p.1): it tests image generators, poses no multiple-choice questions and measures no factual recall (pp.3-6). The generalist suite the sentence names is BIG-bench (Srivastava et al.), a different work. The printed author list does not match either: the paper has ten authors, Hanjun Luo, Haoyu Huang, Ziye Deng, Ruizhe Chen, Xinfeng Li, Hewei Wang, Yingbin Jin, Yang Liu, Wenyuan Xu and Zuozhu Liu (p.1), whereas the reference prints nine names with different first names and no Ruizhe Chen.

suggested_wording: Not for the revised related work. If ever cited, accurately: 'BIGbench (Luo et al., 2024) measures social biases of text-to-image models over 47,040 prompts.'
facts_to_cite: title: 'BIGbench: A Unified Benchmark for Evaluating Multi-dimensional Social Biases in Text-to-Image Models' (p.1)
47,040 prompts; 8 text-to-image models and 3 debiasing methods evaluated (p.2, p.6)

overlap_with_engtrace: None of substance. It shares only an automated model-based evaluator validated against human labels (p.6). It has no reasoning task, no engineering content, no gold traces and no step-level evaluation.
notes: Name collision: BIGbench (this paper) versus BIG-bench (srivastava2022bigbench). Luo et al. should leave the reference list in any case. If the authors keep the name BIG-Bench anywhere, the key must become srivastava2022bigbench, but S-E1's 'factual recall via multiple-choice questions' does not fit BIG-bench either (see that review), so the simplest fix is to drop the BIG-Bench example from S-E1.
